issues.description: The Genre struct's primary String field is named differently in the solution than in the problem statement and in its call sites. The problem statement specifies a Genre with a String property named `name` and an optional `subgenre` (problem_statement.md lines 19-20). In the solution implementation (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 39-45) the struct declares `let genreName: String`. Client code and Book construction use `Genre(name: ...)` and access `genre.name` (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift lines 18-21 and 34-36). This naming inconsistency will cause compilation errors and will confuse students about the intended field name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Genre struct's String property name consistent with the problem statement and its usages. Change `let genreName: String` to `let name: String` in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so that the memberwise initializer `Genre(name: ...)` and property access `genre.name` compile and match the specification. Alternatively (less preferred), update all call sites and the problem text to use `genreName` consistently, but aligning to `name` preserves the stated exercise requirements.
